headline: Life sciences company Danaher plans to open an AI-run laboratory in early 2027 to design and test antibodies up to eight times faster.
score_reason: A company plan with the speed claim made by Danaher itself, announced on 7 Oct; one point below the pool score.
importance_line: Drug and biology researchers who buy antibodies and similar tools could get them faster if it works, but the eight-times figure is Danaher's own claim and the lab does not open until 2027.
summary: Healthcare Digital reports that Danaher will open its first AI-powered autonomous lab at its Abcam unit in early 2027, where AI designs antibodies and other molecules used in research and robots then build and test them, feeding the results back to improve the next design. Danaher says this should take researchers from an idea to a validated research reagent up to eight times faster.
notes: Read at Healthcare Digital and Digital Health News because the HPCwire copy was unreadable. Reuters first reported the announcement on 7 Oct (not read).
